topicData.topic: The AI spending-to-revenue gap is real, but nobody building these systems seems to care — or understand what happens when the math finally gets checked
topicData.angle: Your MacBook just got 18% more expensive because four tech companies spent $725 billion on AI data centres last year and made $75 billion back.

postText:
My MacBook just got 18% more expensive.
Not for a new chip. Not a new design. Just because four tech companies are spending $725 billion a year on AI and making $75 billion back.

That gap isn't a secret. Everyone building inside this knows the numbers.

And that's the weird part. It's not denial. It's more like, nobody wants to be the one who stops first. Because stopping means losing. So you keep going and hope someone else figures out the revenue side before the whole thing gets checked.

Sequoia's David Cahn called it "the $600 billion question." Who actually pays for this?

idk, feels like it won't be the VC who blinked last. Or the CEO who greenlit the data centre.

It'll be the person buying a laptop.

The dot-com crash wiped out trillions after $500 billion went into fibre cables that sat 97% unused underground. This is 10x that scale.

Not saying it crashes. Genuinely don't know. But the math is real and someone somewhere is going to check it.
